mediums.label: Chart
mediums.description: Values encoded as position, length, area, colour, or connection.

mediums.label: Map
mediums.description: A spatial claim in which location or geographic shape is part of the evidence.

mediums.label: Photograph
mediums.description: Journalist-supplied photographs with explicit alt text, credit, and rights.

formats.label: Static image
formats.description: A fixed visual designed to be read at rest.

formats.label: Interactive web
formats.description: A self-contained page a reader can interrogate with pointer, touch, or keyboard.

formats.label: Video
formats.description: A short fixed-duration motion build with one controlled reveal.

formats.label: Scroll-driven story
formats.description: A fixed visual that changes through explicit prose-led scroll steps.

capabilities.label: Restricted live-map delivery

capabilities.label: Datawrapper production

capabilities.label: Hosted embed delivery
capabilities.unavailableReason: Hosted embed delivery needs a verified Cloudflare token and the confirmed newsroom account ID.

interaction.promise: A fixed chart that states its evidence without reader interaction.
Every reading can expose an exact value by hover, tap, or keyboard while the static argument remains readable without JavaScript.
A fixed-duration build reveals one argument in a controlled order and ends on a readable held frame.
An opaque prose card advances a fixed chart through explicit steps while the page scrolls.
A fixed map with one baked camera and a complete legend.
A reader can move through the map, retrieve exact values by pointer or keyboard, and use a linear accessible table; a baked fallback remains without JavaScript.
A fixed camera and geometry build one spatial argument in a controlled order and hold the complete map at the end.
Prose-led steps advance one fixed map while the live layer remains leashed to the subject and the baked fallback remains available.
A fixed, uncropped photograph sequence with journalist-supplied words, alt text, and credit.
Journalist-supplied photographs advance through explicit prose-led steps without automatic description or cropping.

treatments.label: Area (and stacked area)

dataShape.summary: One or more numeric series along a shared ordered axis; stacked areas also require a meaningful additive total.

treatments.purpose: A single-series area chart is a line chart with the space beneath it filled.

treatments.label: Bar and column

dataShape.summary: One numeric value per category measured from a shared baseline.

treatments.purpose: One value per category, encoded as the LENGTH of a rectangle from a shared baseline.

treatments.label: Beeswarm

dataShape.summary: Raw observations with one numeric measure; optional groups must preserve every observation.

treatments.purpose: A beeswarm shows every raw observation on one shared value axis, with no aggregation and no overlap — the "show your data" distribution chart.

treatments.label: Box plot

dataShape.summary: A distribution, or a valid five-number summary, for each category.

treatments.purpose: A box plot compresses a distribution into a five-number summary — minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum — and draws it as a box with whiskers, one per category.

treatments.label: Bullet

dataShape.summary: An actual value and a comparable target for each measure, with optional ordered performance ranges.

treatments.purpose: A bullet chart answers "did this hit its target" for one or more measures, each on its own row: a single bar grows from zero to the actual value, a tick mark shows the target it was measured against, and a neutral backdrop can carry qualitative zones (poor / ok / good) behind the bar.

treatments.label: Bump (ranking-over-time)

dataShape.summary: Ranks for multiple named entities at each point on an ordered axis.

treatments.purpose: A bump chart answers "who overtook whom, and when" among several competitors ranked over multiple periods — a league table's season, a chart's weekly top-ten, a poll's changing front-runners.

treatments.label: Calendar heatmap

dataShape.summary: A real date and numeric value for each observed day.

treatments.purpose: A calendar heatmap answers "when, across a real calendar, did this value run high or low" by laying one cell per day into a fixed weekday-by-week grid and colouring each cell by its value — the same value-to-colour idea as a matrix heatmap, but with the grid's structure fixed to the calendar itself rather than free to be any two categorical axes.

treatments.label: Connected scatter

dataShape.summary: Two numeric measures and an explicit order for every observation in one path.

treatments.purpose: A connected scatter answers "what path did these two measures trace together, over time" — unlike a plain scatter, whose points have no inherent order, here each point IS ordered (usually by time) and the points are joined into a single path, so loops, reversals, and doubling-back all become visible shapes instead of a static cloud.

treatments.label: Diverging bar

dataShape.summary: One signed numeric value per category around a meaningful zero.

treatments.purpose: A diverging bar answers "who gained and who lost, and by how much" for a set of categories whose values are SIGNED — net job change by sector, vote swing by district, temperature anomaly by year.

treatments.label: Diverging stacked bar (Likert)

dataShape.summary: Ordered response shares for each item, including an explicit neutral category where one exists.

treatments.purpose: A diverging stacked bar answers "how did opinion split, for many items at once, when the response scale itself has a neutral middle" — a survey's strongly-disagree-to-strongly-agree results, one row per question, segments stacked outward from a shared centre instead of from a shared zero.

treatments.label: Dot strip

dataShape.summary: Raw numeric observations grouped into named categories.

treatments.purpose: A dot strip lays one horizontal lane per category and marks every raw observation in that category as a dot positioned by its own value, with a small deterministic jitter and enough transparency that overlapping points still show through each other — plus one neutral tick per lane marking that category's mean.

treatments.label: Dumbbell (range plot)

dataShape.summary: Exactly two comparable numeric values for each category.

treatments.purpose: A dumbbell chart answers "how big is the gap between two values, for each of several categories, and which categories have the biggest gap" — one row per category, two dots (one per series) joined by a connecting line whose LENGTH is the point.

treatments.label: Gantt

dataShape.summary: A named item with a valid start and end on one shared time scale.

treatments.purpose: A Gantt chart draws each item as a bar spanning its own start to its own end on one shared, to-scale time axis, one row per item — answering "when did this happen, how long did it take, and what overlapped with what." That's a job a plain event timeline can't do: a timeline of instants can show WHEN something happened but has no way to show DURATION or overlap between concurrent items; a Gantt bar's length is specifically standing in for elapsed time, which is the one thing this type exists to make visible.

treatments.label: Grouped bar

dataShape.summary: A small fixed set of comparable numeric series repeated across categories.

treatments.purpose: A small number of series placed side by side within each category, so a reader can make two comparisons off one chart: within a group (this series here against that one, same category) and across groups (this series here against itself over there, a different category).

treatments.label: Heatmap (matrix)

dataShape.summary: Two categorical or temporal dimensions and one numeric value per cell.

treatments.purpose: A heatmap lays a grid across two categorical (or temporal) dimensions — day by hour, region by year — and encodes a third, quantitative value as the colour of each cell.

treatments.label: Histogram

dataShape.summary: Raw observations of one continuous numeric variable, or explicitly defined contiguous bins.

treatments.purpose: A histogram bins one continuous variable into contiguous intervals and draws a bar per bin whose height is the count that landed there.

treatments.label: Line

dataShape.summary: One or more numeric series on a shared ordered axis, usually time.

treatments.purpose: A continuous series read against an ordered axis, almost always time, encoded as position and joined into a single stroke that reads as one trend.

treatments.label: Lollipop

dataShape.summary: One non-negative numeric magnitude per category from a meaningful zero baseline.

treatments.purpose: A lollipop chart is a bar chart's thin sibling: same job (rank or compare a magnitude per category), same baseline-at-zero rule, same everything about the encoding — just a thin stem and a dot standing in for the solid rectangle.

treatments.label: Marimekko (mosaic plot)

dataShape.summary: Group shares of a grand total plus each group's internal part-to-whole composition.

treatments.purpose: A Marimekko shows two nested part-to-whole proportions at once: column WIDTH encodes each group's share of the grand total, and the segments stacked inside each column encode that group's own internal composition — so a single cell's AREA is the joint share, group-size × internal-split, in one glance.

treatments.label: Parallel coordinates

dataShape.summary: Several numeric variables measured for every item, with an explicit scale for each axis.

treatments.purpose: Parallel coordinates lay several variables out as parallel vertical axes, each keeping its OWN independent scale, with one item drawn as a single polyline crossing every axis in turn — so the crossing pattern of many items' lines reveals trade-offs a table of the same numbers hides: an item that's high on one axis and low on the next shows up as a visibly steep diagonal, and a cluster of similarly-shaped items shows up as a bundle of near-parallel lines.

treatments.label: Pictogram (isotype)

dataShape.summary: A non-negative count and an explicit units-per-icon conversion that does not encode value by icon size.

treatments.purpose: A pictogram states a magnitude as a countable row of equal-size icons, where ONE icon always stands for a stated number of units and count — never icon size — carries the value.

treatments.label: Pie and donut

dataShape.summary: A small number of non-negative parts that exhaust one fixed whole.

treatments.purpose: A pie (or donut — same chart, a hole in the middle and a total in it) answers exactly one question: of a fixed whole, what share does each part hold, when there are few enough parts that the reader can hold all of them in view at once.

treatments.label: Population pyramid

dataShape.summary: Exactly two comparable groups measured across the same ordered bands.

treatments.purpose: A population pyramid is two back-to-back bar charts sharing a central category axis: ordered bands run up the middle, one group's bars extend left, the other's right, each bar's length a magnitude on the same scale.

treatments.label: Radar (spider)

dataShape.summary: The same numeric variables and compatible radial scales for a small number of items.

treatments.purpose: A radar chart plots several variables as axes radiating from a shared centre, each on the SAME radial scale, with one item's readings across all axes joined into a closed polygon — so the shape of that polygon is the read: a balanced item draws a regular shape, a lopsided one draws a spiky or lobsided one.

treatments.label: Sankey

dataShape.summary: Directed flows between ordered stages with non-negative magnitudes and conserved meaning.

treatments.purpose: A sankey diagram answers "how does a quantity flow and split as it moves through a sequence of stages" — energy from source to sector, users from signup to churn, a budget from allocation to spend — with each stage laid out as its own column of nodes and ribbons flowing between them whose THICKNESS is proportional to the amount flowing.

treatments.label: Scatter (and bubble)

dataShape.summary: Two continuous numeric measures for every observation; a bubble variant needs a third positive size measure.

treatments.purpose: A scatter plot answers one question: as one continuous variable moves, what happens to another, across every unit at once.

treatments.label: Slope (slopegraph)

dataShape.summary: Exactly two comparable moments for each named category.

treatments.purpose: A slope chart answers "who moved, in which direction, and by how much, between exactly two moments" — for many categories at once.

treatments.label: Small multiples

dataShape.summary: A repeatable chart schema across facets that can share scales or explicitly disclose scale differences.

treatments.purpose: Small multiples isn't a chart type — it's a layout decision: instead of forcing every group into one crowded chart, repeat the same small chart once per category, panel after panel, all built the same way.

treatments.label: Stacked bar

dataShape.summary: Additive numeric series within each category, where both the total and composition are meaningful.

treatments.purpose: Several series summed into one bar per category, so a single mark carries both the total (the bar's full length) and the composition (each segment's own length within it).

treatments.label: Streamgraph

dataShape.summary: Several non-negative series over an ordered axis where overall rhythm matters more than exact lookup.

treatments.purpose: A streamgraph shows many overlapping time series stacked with no fixed baseline — bands can wiggle up and down around a shifting centre rather than growing from a flat zero line — so the READ is the overall rhythm and relative flow of many series at once, not the exact value of any one band at any one point.

treatments.label: Treemap

dataShape.summary: Non-negative parts nested in meaningful groups, with values that sum within the hierarchy.

treatments.purpose: A treemap answers "how does a total break down, when the pieces ALSO belong to groups worth keeping together" — area encodes each item's value, and items sharing a group are laid out as contiguous tiles, so the group itself reads as a visible region of the frame, not just a shared colour scattered across the page.

treatments.label: Waterfall (bridge)

dataShape.summary: A starting total, an ordered sequence of signed deltas, and an arithmetically consistent ending total.

treatments.purpose: A waterfall chart shows how a starting total arrives at an ending total through a sequence of signed steps — a revenue build, a budget variance, an opening-to-closing balance.

treatments.label: Cartogram

dataShape.summary: Region geometry, adjacency that matters to the story, and a non-negative value used to distort area.

treatments.purpose: A cartogram answers "how big is this region's VALUE," honestly, by distorting each region's own area to be proportional to a number — trading recognisable geography for magnitude a reader can compare at a glance.

treatments.label: Choropleth

dataShape.summary: Joinable named-region geometry and a normalized rate, share, or intensity rather than a raw count.

treatments.purpose: A choropleth answers "which of these named regions is proportionally worse or better off," where the regions are a partition the reader already recognises — countries, states, districts.

treatments.label: Contour / isoline

dataShape.summary: Dense georeferenced samples of a genuinely continuous field, sufficient to justify interpolation.

treatments.disabledReason: The doctrine reference is retained, but Splash has no shipped contour/isoline implementation; choose a supported map treatment instead.
treatments.purpose: A contour (isoline) map answers "where does this continuous field cross a given value" — elevation, temperature, air pressure, rainfall, travel-time-from-a-point — by drawing lines that connect every point sharing the same value, the way topographic elevation lines do.

treatments.label: Dot density

dataShape.summary: Joinable region polygons and non-negative totals whose within-region dot positions are explicitly synthetic.

treatments.purpose: A dot-density map answers "where inside these regions is this concentrated" — population, cases, production — at a texture level: dense clusters of dots read as dense clusters of the thing, sparse areas read as sparse, without forcing the reader to decode a single number per region the way a choropleth does.

treatments.label: Flow map (route)

dataShape.summary: One ordered route geometry or waypoint sequence whose path and direction are part of the claim.

treatments.purpose: A flow/route map answers "what path did this take, and what did it pass through, in order" — a ship's voyage, a migration corridor, an evacuation route, a supply chain's journey — where the sequence of places crossed is itself part of the claim, not just the endpoints.

treatments.label: Hex grid (spatial binning)

dataShape.summary: Enough raw georeferenced events to support spatial aggregation into a regular grid.

treatments.purpose: A hex-grid map answers "where is this cluster of scattered EVENTS actually densest," by aggregating raw points — incidents, sightings, transactions — into a regular grid of cells so the eye sees a smooth density surface instead of an unreadable smear of thousands of overlapping dots.

treatments.label: Locator

dataShape.summary: Named point locations with valid coordinates and optional categories, but no value encoded by marker size.

treatments.purpose: A locator answers "where, exactly" — it names a set of places relevant to the story (the sites of an event, the stops on an itinerary, the hometowns of people quoted) with nothing more than position and, optionally, a category.

treatments.label: Proportional symbol (symbol / bubble map)

dataShape.summary: Named point locations with valid coordinates and a positive numeric magnitude at each place.

treatments.purpose: A proportional symbol map answers "how big is this quantity AT this specific place" — a city's population, an earthquake's magnitude, a plant's output — where the geography is a set of POINTS, not a partition of area.

treatments.label: Photograph sequence

dataShape.summary: Journalist-supplied image files in an explicit order, each with rights, alt text, caption, and credit supplied by the journalist.

treatments.purpose: Journalist-supplied image files in an explicit order, each with rights, alt text, caption, and credit supplied by the journalist.
